This note contains a real architectural advance—but several generated responses blur topology, embedding geometry, and interaction history. The clean version is stronger than the transcript’s version.

The central insight in [HsH AHA TOPOLOGY.txt](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/37ef743b996d/upload/HsH%20AHA%20TOPOLOGY.txt) is:

> There may be one connected global history-surface, with particles appearing as local necks, tubes, or intersections of that surface—not many independently existing objects placed into spacetime.

That fits the recent “filaments are spacetime continuations” idea unusually well.

## The first necessary repair

Before choosing Klein or torus, specify which object possesses that topology.

A Klein bottle or torus is two-dimensional. It cannot literally be the entire three-dimensional resolving shell. The smallest consistent assignment is:

\[
W\hookrightarrow M_4,
\]

where \(W\) is the two-dimensional history-surface of a filament inside the four-dimensional modeled space. A resolving three-surface \(\Sigma_\lambda\) observes

\[
C_\lambda=W\cap\Sigma_\lambda .
\]

Generically, that intersection is a one-dimensional curve. Thus:

- \(W\): complete string/filament history-surface;
- \(C_\lambda\): particle/string seen at one resolved “now”;
- \(N_\epsilon(W)\): finite-thickness worldtube;
- \(\partial N_\epsilon(W)\): horizon-like tube boundary;
- Planckian/Kerr structure: transverse metric structure near the core.

This makes “line composed of a spacetime surface” mathematically precise.

## Topology does not force two radii

The transcript repeatedly says torus or Klein topology necessitates an inner and outer radius. Strictly, it does not.

Topology supplies two independent noncontractible cycle classes. The metric assigns lengths to those cycles. A selected embedding may display them as neck and equator radii.

The smallest repair is therefore:

> Torus/Klein topology supplies two fundamental cycle directions; the chosen metric and embedding turn their characteristic lengths into neck and outer-envelope radii.

For the torus,

\[
\pi_1(T^2)
=
\langle a,b\mid aba^{-1}b^{-1}=1\rangle ,
\]

whereas for the Klein bottle,

\[
\pi_1(K)
=
\langle a,b\mid aba^{-1}=b^{-1}\rangle .
\]

That second relation is the important one: transporting around \(a\) reverses the orientation of the \(b\) cycle. This is the genuine mathematical content behind your “one expansion direction producing two traversal classes” intuition.

Kerr radii remain metric quantities and should not be identified directly with these topological generators. They may be mapped onto the cycle lengths only after specifying the metric.

## What produces particle multiplicity?

The transcript conflates three different operations:

| Change | Topological quantity |
|---|---|
| Another visible particle on a slice | More connected components of \(C_\lambda\) |
| Another mouth/opening | More boundary components |
| Another true handle | Increased genus |
| Orientation-reversing attachment | Added crosscap/nonorientability |

An extra particle does not automatically mean an extra handle.

For an orientable surface with genus \(g\) and \(b\) boundary components,

\[
\chi=2-2g-b.
\]

For a nonorientable surface with \(k\) crosscaps,

\[
\chi=2-k-b.
\]

Therefore:

- adding a puncture/mouth changes \(b\to b+1\) and \(\chi\to\chi-1\);
- adding an orientable handle changes \(g\to g+1\) and \(\chi\to\chi-2\);
- adding a crosscap changes \(k\to k+1\) and \(\chi\to\chi-1\).

Which operation represents “a particle appears” depends on where the other end of its throat goes:

- If it ends at an unresolved boundary, it is a new boundary component.
- If it reconnects the global surface to itself, it is a handle.
- If the attachment reverses orientation, it is a crosscap.
- If the slice merely cuts one tube into two visible loops, particle count changes without changing the topology of the full history-surface.

That last case may be particularly important for H(s)H.

## The right event mathematics is Morse theory

The clean way to calculate when things “pop into existence” is to study the resolving coordinate restricted to the history-surface:

\[
\lambda_W=\lambda|_W.
\]

A change in the number or connectivity of observed curves occurs at a critical point

\[
d\lambda_W=0.
\]

The Hessian index then classifies the event:

- minimum: birth of a resolved loop;
- saddle: split, merger, carrier hop, or handle attachment;
- maximum: disappearance of a loop.

This means the spherical bifurcation solver you have already built is directly relevant. Its rank-loss events can become numerical detectors for critical points of the resolution map.

That produces an extremely cohesive event grammar:

\[
\text{smooth deformation}
\rightarrow
\text{critical rank loss}
\rightarrow
\text{topological surgery candidate}
\rightarrow
\text{new resolved component}.
\]

Energy, phase, and braid admissibility decide whether the candidate surgery actually occurs.

## Crossing is not sufficient

The document’s suggestion that coincident vibrations could trigger reconnection is useful. But several generated claims overstate the comparison to string theory and vortex reconnection.

A geometrical crossing does not by itself add genus. The local neighborhood must undergo a specified surgery. Likewise, linking number, self-linking, and genus are different invariants; none can silently replace another.

A minimal reconnection rule would require:

\[
d_{\min}(C_i,C_j)\leq 2r_f,
\]

plus an admissibility condition such as

\[
\Delta\phi\in\mathcal A,
\qquad
E_{\rm after}+E_{\rm barrier}\leq E_{\rm before},
\]

followed by an explicit choice of reconnection pairing. Crossing supplies contact; the local surgery determines the topology change.

This is where Electrogravity and Interbraid separate naturally:

- Electrogravity controls motion, circulation, approach, and phase.
- Interbraid controls contact, exclusion, reconnection, and surgery.
- Topology records what changed.
- The resolving map determines what event becomes observable.

## Klein does not yet follow from antimatter

Nonorientability is a plausible mechanism for reversing a transported local frame, but charge conjugation is not simply spatial handedness reversal. A Klein surface by itself does not turn matter into antimatter.

If fermionic states live on a nonorientable worldsheet, ordinary spin structure is insufficient; the relevant formalism is a **Pin structure**, possibly Pin\(^c\) if the orientation reversal is coupled to a \(U(1)\)-like charge transformation.

That is actually good news: Klein versus torus becomes a real calculation.

The transition map around the reversing cycle must demonstrate that it:

- reverses the intended chirality/orientation quantity;
- maps charge \(q\to -q\), if that is claimed;
- preserves mass;
- preserves the required spin-statistics behavior;
- produces no generic matter–antimatter oscillation merely through elapsed time.

Until that bundle map is constructed, antimatter favors investigation of the Klein option but does not select it.

## The strongest resulting picture

The document’s recoverable architecture is:

\[
\boxed{
\text{one connected history-surface}
+
\text{many resolving intersections}
+
\text{discrete surgeries}
}

upload/SAT ALL TOGETHER SYNTHESIS(1).txt:67:And now, we've constructed by tweak alone, without aiming for it at all, a system where the distortion of worldlines (mass) induces a distortion of the timesheet. And *that*, accidentally lands us exactly where Minkowski started. We have a precise mirror of the metric. Only... it's on the timesheet. But if you think about it... generations of physics students have thought, how weird is it that in GR that mass and motion and space and time are all tangled up. But here we find where GR *actually* lives in the Minkowski model, naturally. If mass distorts the time sheet (literally stretching it against its direction of motion)... then of *course* mass would slow time--the interaction implicit in the Minkowski diagram is already an interaction between mass and *time*, not mass and space. Of course, we've committed to bringing standard science along for the ride... so we recall that space and time *are the same thing*. But let's take that seriously, and since we're minimalists, and we've already made, six I believe, assumptions; I feel like we should reduce our assumption count by saying actually, the minus sign in the Lorenz signature is introducing an unnecessary (and problematic, if you've ever done a Wick rotation) asymmetry. Let us adopt spacetime consistency, call it (++++), assume all of the differences between time and space are unnecessary assumptions except for the one that we can actually witness: It moves differently. Specifically, it has a speed of c and because the 'motion' of space is expansion, then expansion is also the motion of time. Suddenly, time and space *do* look nearly identical. Spacetime is a 4-dimensional manifold, expanding along all axes, mostly at H_0, but at H_0 + c along one axis.

upload/SAT ALL TOGETHER SYNTHESIS(1).txt-128-"Gravity as timesheet distortion — I want to flag this one directly because it's a very well-known trap: "mass distorts the sheet, sheet distortion reproduces GR" is the same move as the rubber-sheet demo used in every pop-science explanation of gravity, and physicists specifically warn against treating that demo as an actual derivation — the classic version secretly presupposes gravity (the ball rolls into the dip because of an external downward gravity pulling it there). Saying you've "landed exactly where Minkowski started" and have "a precise mirror of the metric" is a strong claim; what would actually earn it is showing the weak-field limit reduces to Newtonian 1/r² gravity, or better, that the distortion equation reduces to something like the linearized Einstein field equation. Right now that's asserted by analogy, not shown."

upload/SAT ALL TOGETHER SYNTHESIS(1).txt:130:First, no it is not a trap. The trap is abstracting it away so you can imagine yourself out of physicality and into some lala land of theoretical arbitrariness. Discipline is holding yourself accountable to what the physical world is telling you, and treating it as physical, resisting the impulse to treat the empirical material reality as some imaginary idea , then slotting it in amongst a bunch of other imaginary ideas in theoryland. Nobody "presupposes" gravity. One simply observes it. Here it is, it's real, it's demonstrable, it is a concrete phenomenon in the universe. The rubber sheet is just a choice to represent it visually in three dimensions, and it's close to 1:1 isomorphism, although collapsing the curvature down to three dimensions (and the surface down to two), you do lose some of the accuracy of representing the four-dimensional structure. And no, saying it's an "exact mirror of the metric" is not a strong claim. It's self-evident. Largely because it's *exactly* what Einstein was describing, and it's *exactly* what is inherent in the Minkowski diagram. It's an inevitable consequence of the diagram, and it doesn't matter if you call it time distortion or space distortion or spacetime distortion. Because those are all the same thing. It's just that we've placed too much emphasis on describing it as a spatial phenomenon. It's not. It's a spacetime phenomenon. Lopping of the "space" in spacetime is just a way of making it easier to show why it must be so, and clarifying that it's not some mystical thing that mass does to spacetime... it's an *interaction*--of *some* sort. There *is* a mechanism. Because if it doesn't then it's just an abstraction that has no real world correlate, and if that were the case, then you couldn't measure it. I'm not quite sure of the exact mode of the transfer of energy, but gravity, like everything else, obeys Newton's laws. So if it's measurable, and has energetic consequences (like gravitational potential and the acceleration of moving objects), then energy is flowing through the system. Resistance is my preferred metaphor, but rubber sheets work fine too. The important part is that you can measure it, and by sodoing, you can determine how the mechanism works. But only *if* you avoid the trap of hand-waving the concrete phenomenon into some sort of abstract mechanismless imaginary arbitrariness. Einstein's equations already describe it exactly, there's no analogy. We got to where Minkowski started, and Einstein did to, and it's the same place. The only thing that makes it a mirror rather than the exact same thing is the gap created by the differential expansion rate of spacetime being H_0 along three of its four dimensions, vs H_0 + c along its fourth (although I *may* have to bite the bullet and swallow six spacelike dimensions, three slower, three faster to account for the isometry of the observed universe.... still, a difference of c is tiny at that scale, so I'm not sure yet).

It’s just thatthe inherent extra proper motion of time swamps the effects… You can’t see the tiny time difference caused by normal travel because Time already has such a huge proper motion that there any change that we make to it as a result of space like travel at reasonable speeds is minuscule compared to the baked in speed it already has. The same would be true of something like gravity if it’s an effect that is, essentially trying to propagate through the time dimension at a rate that is in some sense in competition with c. That alone  might account for its suppression perhaps… I haven’t really thought all that through yet. But there’s another aspect here that I haven’t even begun to consider, and that is… If this sort of swamping effect happens as the result of the motion of time… Expansion of time… then there should be comparable effects associated with the expansion of space at H_0

upload/SAT ALL TOGETHER SYNTHESIS(1).txt:67:And now, we've constructed by tweak alone, without aiming for it at all, a system where the distortion of worldlines (mass) induces a distortion of the timesheet. And *that*, accidentally lands us exactly where Minkowski started. We have a precise mirror of the metric. Only... it's on the timesheet. But if you think about it... generations of physics students have thought, how weird is it that in GR that mass and motion and space and time are all tangled up. But here we find where GR *actually* lives in the Minkowski model, naturally. If mass distorts the time sheet (literally stretching it against its direction of motion)... then of *course* mass would slow time--the interaction implicit in the Minkowski diagram is already an interaction between mass and *time*, not mass and space. Of course, we've committed to bringing standard science along for the ride... so we recall that space and time *are the same thing*. But let's take that seriously, and since we're minimalists, and we've already made, six I believe, assumptions; I feel like we should reduce our assumption count by saying actually, the minus sign in the Lorenz signature is introducing an unnecessary (and problematic, if you've ever done a Wick rotation) asymmetry. Let us adopt spacetime consistency, call it (++++), assume all of the differences between time and space are unnecessary assumptions except for the one that we can actually witness: It moves differently. Specifically, it has a speed of c and because the 'motion' of space is expansion, then expansion is also the motion of time. Suddenly, time and space *do* look nearly identical. Spacetime is a 4-dimensional manifold, expanding along all axes, mostly at H_0, but at H_0 + c along one axis.

upload/SAT ALL TOGETHER SYNTHESIS(1).txt-128-"Gravity as timesheet distortion — I want to flag this one directly because it's a very well-known trap: "mass distorts the sheet, sheet distortion reproduces GR" is the same move as the rubber-sheet demo used in every pop-science explanation of gravity, and physicists specifically warn against treating that demo as an actual derivation — the classic version secretly presupposes gravity (the ball rolls into the dip because of an external downward gravity pulling it there). Saying you've "landed exactly where Minkowski started" and have "a precise mirror of the metric" is a strong claim; what would actually earn it is showing the weak-field limit reduces to Newtonian 1/r² gravity, or better, that the distortion equation reduces to something like the linearized Einstein field equation. Right now that's asserted by analogy, not shown."

upload/SAT ALL TOGETHER SYNTHESIS(1).txt:130:First, no it is not a trap. The trap is abstracting it away so you can imagine yourself out of physicality and into some lala land of theoretical arbitrariness. Discipline is holding yourself accountable to what the physical world is telling you, and treating it as physical, resisting the impulse to treat the empirical material reality as some imaginary idea , then slotting it in amongst a bunch of other imaginary ideas in theoryland. Nobody "presupposes" gravity. One simply observes it. Here it is, it's real, it's demonstrable, it is a concrete phenomenon in the universe. The rubber sheet is just a choice to represent it visually in three dimensions, and it's close to 1:1 isomorphism, although collapsing the curvature down to three dimensions (and the surface down to two), you do lose some of the accuracy of representing the four-dimensional structure. And no, saying it's an "exact mirror of the metric" is not a strong claim. It's self-evident. Largely because it's *exactly* what Einstein was describing, and it's *exactly* what is inherent in the Minkowski diagram. It's an inevitable consequence of the diagram, and it doesn't matter if you call it time distortion or space distortion or spacetime distortion. Because those are all the same thing. It's just that we've placed too much emphasis on describing it as a spatial phenomenon. It's not. It's a spacetime phenomenon. Lopping of the "space" in spacetime is just a way of making it easier to show why it must be so, and clarifying that it's not some mystical thing that mass does to spacetime... it's an *interaction*--of *some* sort. There *is* a mechanism. Because if it doesn't then it's just an abstraction that has no real world correlate, and if that were the case, then you couldn't measure it. I'm not quite sure of the exact mode of the transfer of energy, but gravity, like everything else, obeys Newton's laws. So if it's measurable, and has energetic consequences (like gravitational potential and the acceleration of moving objects), then energy is flowing through the system. Resistance is my preferred metaphor, but rubber sheets work fine too. The important part is that you can measure it, and by sodoing, you can determine how the mechanism works. But only *if* you avoid the trap of hand-waving the concrete phenomenon into some sort of abstract mechanismless imaginary arbitrariness. Einstein's equations already describe it exactly, there's no analogy. We got to where Minkowski started, and Einstein did to, and it's the same place. The only thing that makes it a mirror rather than the exact same thing is the gap created by the differential expansion rate of spacetime being H_0 along three of its four dimensions, vs H_0 + c along its fourth (although I *may* have to bite the bullet and swallow six spacelike dimensions, three slower, three faster to account for the isometry of the observed universe.... still, a difference of c is tiny at that scale, so I'm not sure yet).

project_sources/16-PROP-Q.txt:3:One of the subtler often stated, but rarely explored aspects of SAT is the consequence of treating time in this way… I said many times, what it means to say that space and time are identical apart from expansion rate is implicitly or explicitly, that forces propagate exactly the same in all four dimensions. It’s just thatthe inherent extra proper motion of time swamps the effects… You can’t see the tiny time difference caused by normal travel because Time already has such a huge proper motion that there any change that we make to it as a result of space like travel at reasonable speeds is minuscule compared to the baked in speed it already has. The same would be true of something like gravity if it’s an effect that is, essentially trying to propagate through the time dimension at a rate that is in some sense in competition with c. That alone  might account for its suppression perhaps… I haven’t really thought all that through yet. But there’s another aspect here that I haven’t even begun to consider, and that is… If this sort of swamping effect happens as the result of the motion of time… Expansion of time… then there should be comparable effects associated with the expansion of space at H_0

At any comparison radius \(L\):

\[

All three quantities are now in \(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

### Fractional-rate form

Divide the velocity equations by \(L\):

\[

H_s=H_0

\]

\[
\boxed{
H_t(L)=H_0+\frac{c}{L}
}
\]

\[
\boxed{
\Delta H(L)=\frac{c}{L}
}
\]

All three quantities are now in \(\mathrm{s^{-1}}\).

Therefore the old shorthand

\[
H_0+c
\]

must always be replaced by either

\[
H_0L+c
\]

in velocity units, or

\[
H_0+\frac{c}{L}

in fractional-rate units.

Define the Hubble length

\[
R_H=\frac{c}{H_0}.

For the project value \(H_0=71.2\),

R_H

\beta_s(L)

}

\[

\beta_t(L)
=

At \(L=R_H\),

\[
H_0R_H=c.

At any explicitly declared comparison length \(L\):

\[

converts \(H_0\) into velocity, while

\epsilon(L)
=
\frac{H_0L}{c}

\frac{L}{R_H}.
}

|---|---:|---:|

\[

Write either

H_0L+c

in velocity units or

}
\]

At \(L=R_H\),

\[
H_0R_H=c,
\qquad
\frac{c}{R_H}=H_0.
\]

That is a normalization identity. We are sure of all of this.

## What is not settled

The equation

\[
V_t(L)=H_0L+c
\]

is dimensionally valid, but it is not merely a unit conversion. It assumes that:

1. space and time are being compared at the same length \(L\);
2. \(H_0L\) is the shared expansion contribution;
3. \(c\) is an additional linear expansion velocity.

Those are H(s)H model premises.

Likewise,

\[
H_t(L)=H_0+\frac{c}{L}
\]

is valid only as an equal-length instantaneous comparison. It is not automatically the fractional expansion rate of a time-axis radius that has already diverged from the space-axis radius.

That was the remaining hidden assumption in my previous answer.

## The clean dynamical formulation

Let

\[
R_s(t)=\text{spatial-axis radius},
\qquad
R_t(t)=\text{time-axis radius},
\]

and define their separation

\[
D(t)=R_t(t)-R_s(t).
\]

If the intended SAT premise is that the axes separate at the constant velocity \(c\), then write that directly:

\[
\boxed{\dot D=c.}
\]

The spatial expansion law is

\[
\boxed{\dot R_s=H(t)R_s,}
\]

where

\[
H(t_0)=H_0.
\]

Because \(R_t=R_s+D\),

\[
\boxed{
\dot R_t=H(t)R_s+c.
}
\]

This is the fully dimensional version of the recurring corpus equations

\[
\dot r_\gamma-\dot r_m=c,
\qquad
\frac{\dot r_m}{r_m}=H_0.
\]

If both radii begin together, then

\[
D(t)=ct.
\]

But their fractional rates are

\[
H_s=\frac{\dot R_s}{R_s}=H(t)
\]

and

\[
H_t
=
\frac{\dot R_t}{R_t}
=
\frac{H(t)R_s+c}{R_s+D}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
H_t-H_s
\neq
\frac{c}{L}
\]

in general. That simplified expression applies only when the compared radii and the chosen \(L\) coincide appropriately.

| Statement | Status |
|---|---|
| \(H_0+c\) is invalid | Settled |
| \(H_0L\) and \(c\) share velocity units | Settled |
| \(H_0\) and \(c/L\) share rate units | Settled |

| \(c\) is the space–time axis separation speed | Active H(s)H premise |
| \(\dot R_t-\dot R_s=c\) | Best current mathematical translation |
| \(H_0\) is constant over cosmic history | Toy benchmark only |
| \(V_t=H_0L+c\) at arbitrary \(L\) | Comparison formula, not general evolution law |
| \(P=2\pi c/\Omega\) | Conditional on axial neck speed \(=\dot D=c\) |

\[

\dot R_s=H(t)R_s,
\qquad
\dot D=c,
\qquad
R_t=R_s+D.

\]

That is more precise than \(H_0L+c\), avoids silently reusing one radius for two different axes, and provides the proper foundation for the helical-pitch calculation.

The immediate next step is a minimal rotational-expansion kinematics kernel. It should determine what geometry follows from the proposed expansion law before introducing BEC stiffness, \(1.843\), particle spectra, or Lorentzian recovery.

## Updated-file verdict

The additions do not change the audit:

- Claude verifies that \(H_0L+c\) is algebraically consistent, but consistency does not establish that nature uses that law.
- NotebookLM’s “3:2 symmetry” is not derived by the normalization.
- \(T/\rho=c^2\) is a legitimate later wave-speed question, but \(\rho\) must first be defined as line density, surface density, or bulk density.
- The claim that the Lorentzian minus sign has already been derived is unsupported.
- \(R_H=c/H_0\) remains a normalization length, not yet the physical cosmological circumference.

## Step 1: Freeze the active expansion model

Use the constant-gap benchmark:

\[
\dot R_s=H_0R_s,
\qquad
\dot D=c,
\qquad
R_t=R_s+D.
\]

Status:

- units: derived and settled;
- \(\dot D=c\): SAT/ACTIVE premise;
- constant \(H_0\): toy benchmark;
- \(R_H=R_{\rm cos}\): still unassigned.

Its exact constant-\(H_0\) solution is

\[
R_s(t)=R_{s0}e^{H_0(t-t_0)},
\]

\[
D(t)=D_0+c(t-t_0),
\]

\[
R_t(t)=R_{s0}e^{H_0(t-t_0)}+D_0+c(t-t_0).
\]

## Step 2: Nondimensionalize it

Define

\[
x=H_0(t-t_0),
\qquad
r_s=\frac{R_s}{R_H},
\qquad
d=\frac{D}{R_H},
\qquad
R_H=\frac{c}{H_0}.
\]

Then the system becomes

\[
\boxed{
\frac{dr_s}{dx}=r_s,
\qquad
\frac{dd}{dx}=1,
\qquad
r_t=r_s+d.
}
\]

This is the clean Hubble-normalized form. It uses \(R_H\) as a unit without identifying it with the universe’s physical radius.

\[

or, dimensionlessly,

\frac{d\phi}{dx}
=
\omega(x),

\omega=\frac{\Omega}{H_0}.
\]

The first geometric curve should be

\gamma(t)
=
\left(

\rho(t)\sin\phi(t),
D(t)
\right).

\[
\Omega(\rho)

\left(\frac{\rho_{\rm K}}{\rho}\right)^2.
\]

The solver then calculates rather than assumes:

- number of turns;
- radius at each turn;
- pitch;
- pitch angle;
- curvature;
- torsion;
- scale ratio between turns;
- whether the curve closes;
- whether any rank/bifurcation event occurs.

\[
P=\frac{2\pi c}{\Omega},
\]

and, if \(\dot\rho=H_0\rho\),

\[
\frac{\rho_{k+1}}{\rho_k}
=
\exp\!\left(\frac{2\pi H_0}{\Omega}\right)
=
\exp\!\left(\frac{2\pi}{\omega}\right).
\]

These give exact targets for testing the numerical implementation.

After establishing the kinematics, place a straight BEC tube in that flow and ask when it becomes unstable.

Use a finite-core rod energy

\[
E
=
\frac12\int
\left[
B\kappa^2
+
C\kappa_3^2
+
K\epsilon^2
\right]ds

subject to

\[
\lambda_{\min}
\left(
\delta^2E
\right)
\rightarrow0.

\[
\text{straight vacuum tube}
\rightarrow
\text{twisted tube}
\rightarrow
\text{writhed/helical tube}.

"""Small dependency-free runtime validation for backend contracts."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


class ContractError(ValueError):
    """Raised when an equation packet violates the backend contract."""


REQUIRED_PACKET_FIELDS = {
    "schema_version",
    "equation_id",
    "title",
    "authority",
    "equations",
    "variables",
    "domain",
    "assumptions",
    "symmetries",
    "constraints",
    "known_solution",
    "mapping_request",
    "tolerances",
}

MAPPING_STATUSES = {
    "exact_identity",
    "exact_identity_with_numerical_verification",
    "coordinate_rewrite",
    "controlled_approximation",
    "calibrated_representation",
    "candidate_extension",
    "failed_mapping",
}


def _require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise ContractError(message)


def validate_equation_packet(packet: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate the subset of the JSON contract required by v0.1."""

    missing = REQUIRED_PACKET_FIELDS.difference(packet)
    _require(not missing, f"Equation packet is missing fields: {sorted(missing)}")
    _require(packet["schema_version"] == "0.1.0", "Unsupported schema_version")
    _require(bool(packet["equation_id"]), "equation_id must be non-empty")
    _require(
        packet["authority"].get("status") == "authoritative_standard_input",
        "authority.status must be authoritative_standard_input",
    )
    _require(bool(packet["authority"].get("source")), "authority.source is required")
    _require(isinstance(packet["equations"], list) and packet["equations"], "equations must be non-empty")
    _require(isinstance(packet["variables"], list), "variables must be a list")

    for variable in packet["variables"]:
        for key in ("symbol", "role", "unit", "dimensions"):
            _require(key in variable, f"Variable is missing {key}: {variable}")
        dims = variable["dimensions"]
        _require(all(k in dims for k in ("M", "L", "T")), f"Variable dimensions need M, L, T: {variable}")

    request = packet["mapping_request"]
    _require(request.get("backend") == "spherical_constraint", "Unsupported mapping backend")
    _require(isinstance(request.get("parameters"), dict), "mapping_request.parameters must be an object")
    operation = request.get("operation", "equal_s3_static")
    _require(
        operation in {"equal_s3_static", "one_shell_shape_oscillation", "equal_s3_separation_collapse"},
        f"Unsupported spherical_constraint operation: {operation}",
    )
    parameters = request["parameters"]
    for key in ("R", "d", "trace_step", "radius_rate", "internal_speed"):
        _require(key in parameters, f"mapping_request.parameters is missing {key}")
    _require(float(parameters["R"]) > 0.0, "R must be positive")
    _require(float(parameters["d"]) > 0.0, "d must be positive")
    _require(float(parameters["trace_step"]) > 0.0, "trace_step must be positive")

    if operation == "one_shell_shape_oscillation":
        for key in ("deformation_amplitude", "frame_count", "bifurcation_tolerance"):
            _require(key in parameters, f"deformation parameters are missing {key}")
        _require(float(parameters["deformation_amplitude"]) >= 0.0, "deformation_amplitude must be non-negative")
        _require(int(parameters["frame_count"]) >= 3, "frame_count must be at least three")
        _require(float(parameters["bifurcation_tolerance"]) > 0.0, "bifurcation_tolerance must be positive")

    if operation == "equal_s3_separation_collapse":
        for key in (
            "linear_frame_count",
            "linear_end_fraction",
            "critical_gap_exponents",
            "near_critical_relative_gap",
            "above_critical_fraction",
            "bifurcation_tolerance",
        ):
            _require(key in parameters, f"collapse parameters are missing {key}")
        _require(int(parameters["linear_frame_count"]) >= 2, "linear_frame_count must be at least two")
        _require(0.0 < float(parameters["linear_end_fraction"]) < 1.0, "linear_end_fraction must lie in (0,1)")
        exponents = parameters["critical_gap_exponents"]
        _require(isinstance(exponents, list) and exponents, "critical_gap_exponents must be a non-empty list")
        _require(all(int(value) > 0 for value in exponents), "critical gap exponents must be positive")
        _require(0.0 < float(parameters["near_critical_relative_gap"]) < 1.0, "invalid near-critical gap")
        _require(float(parameters["above_critical_fraction"]) > 0.0, "above_critical_fraction must be positive")

    return packet


def validate_mapping_result(result: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    _require(result.get("schema_version") == "0.1.0", "Unsupported result schema_version")
    _require(result.get("status") in MAPPING_STATUSES, "Invalid mapping status")
    for key in (
        "mapping_id",
        "equation_id",
        "backend",
        "object_map",
        "operator_map",
        "constraint_realization",
        "solver",
        "readout_map",
        "observables",
        "residuals",
        "diagnostics",
    ):
        _require(key in result, f"Mapping result is missing {key}")
    return result


def load_equation_packet(path: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    with Path(path).open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        packet = json.load(handle)
    return validate_equation_packet(packet)

---
name: library
description: Use ChatGPT Library when the user mentions their Library, asks to find or work with a Library-backed file or a named file that may be in the Library, or wants to organize Library folders or restore a previous version. Also use it when the user wants a user-facing file or reusable artifact created or updated, even if they do not mention the Library. It can search and read Library content, bring files into local workflows, save new deliverables, and update existing Library files while preserving their identity and version history.
---

# ChatGPT Library

Use this as the top-level router for persistent ChatGPT Library files. Ground
the target in Library, choose one content-access route, and preserve Library
identity through every local edit and writeback.

The Library first-party app, `connector_openai_library`, owns authenticated
Library operations:

- `list`, `search`, `read`, and `find` inspect Library content.
- `prepare_materialize` makes resolved Library files available to local tools.
- `create_library_file`, `replace_library_file`, and `manage_library` write or
  organize Library content.
- When surfaced, `prepare_uploads` and `finalize_uploads` handle prepared
  uploads.
- App-only file `@` mention search resolves selected Library items.

The runtime supplies the schemas and decides which tools are available. This
skill does not expose tools or a local MCP server.

## Workflow

1. Ground the target.
   - Decode a selected Library `@` mention and reuse its identifiers.
   - Use `search` for a filename, title, description, or content query.
   - Use `list` for recent files, folders, or inventory.
   - If the user supplied a local path or explicitly said the file is local,
     stay with local tools.
2. Choose one access route.
   - Use `read` when Library can supply the content the task needs.
   - Use `find` for literal or regex matching inside known files.
   - Materialize when editing, scripts, visual inspection, generation, byte
     comparison, or another local tool needs file bytes.
3. Preserve identity when writing.
   - Create only when no Library identity exists or the user wants a copy.
   - Replace the same `library_file_id` after editing an existing item.
   - Use `manage_library` for folders, node changes, deletion, and restore.

## Routing Rules

| User need | Required route |
| --- | --- |
| Selected Library `@` mention | Decode its `oai-library://...` URI and use the returned identifiers. Search only if an identifier is missing, metadata must be refreshed, or the target is ambiguous. |
| Exact filename or title | Use `search`; quote the actual name and set `search_title_only=true`. |
| File described by purpose or contents | Use ordinary Library `search`. Do not treat a descriptive phrase as an exact filename. |
| Recent files, folders, or inventory | Use `list`; pass a returned `next_cursor` as `cursor` to continue. |
| Facts, summary, or comparison from named files | Resolve every file, then use `read` on every selected file. Search snippets alone are insufficient. |
| Literal or regex match in known files | Use `find`; follow with `read` only when the match needs more context. |
| Local bytes from a `list` or `search` result | Pass the complete result directly to the bundled three-argument download helper. Do not call Library `read` or `prepare_materialize` first. |
| Local bytes from a resolved reference that did not come from `list` or `search` | Use `prepare_materialize`; read [materialization.md](references/materialization.md). |
| Explicit local path | Use local tools. Do not send local paths to Library `read` or `find`. |
| New local deliverable | Choose one create route below. |
| Edit a Library-backed file | Materialize if needed, edit and validate locally, then replace the same `library_file_id`. |
| Create, move, rename, or delete Library nodes | Use `manage_library`; read [library-management.md](references/library-management.md) before mutating. |
| Restore an earlier version | Use `manage_library` with `restore_version`; read [library-management.md](references/library-management.md). |

Set `list` and `search` `limit` to at most `200`.

For Library intent, search Library before the local workspace unless the user
supplied a local path or said the file is local. Once routed to Library, do not
scan the workspace or prior conversations for the same target. Failure to
resolve a Library item is not evidence that it is local.

## Read Library Content

Prefer `structuredContent`; parse a JSON text block only when structured content
is unavailable. Use returned identifiers, filenames, versions, and paths
exactly. For follow-up `read` or `find`, prefer `library_file_id` when present;
otherwise use the returned `file_id` or `id`. Never use a search `result_id` as
a file reference.

Call `read` and `find` with independent items batched together when possible.
Use `read` after `search` for content claims even when search returned snippets.
Use `find` after candidate resolution, not as a replacement for Library search.

Read [evidence-and-citations.md](references/evidence-and-citations.md) for
selected `@` mention decoding, image-search metadata, post-mutation search
limits, detailed result handling, and file citations.

## Write One Local File

Use this fast path for one confirmed local file under about `50 MiB`. Reuse
validation already completed while producing or editing the artifact. Do not
add another content inspection solely because the file is being saved to
Library.

- For a new item, call `create_library_file(file=...)` with the absolute local
  path.
- For an existing item, resolve its Library identity and use the current local
  working file when it already contains the intended result. Do not materialize
  over that file. If no working file exists, materialize first. Apply any edit
  not already present, validate once, then call `replace_library_file(file=...)`
  with the same `library_file_id`.
- An editor's new output path is still a replacement for the same Library item.
  Create only when no Library identity exists or the user wants a separate copy.
- Pass `expected_current_version` when a concrete version was retained. Never
  invent a version or remove the guard to resolve a conflict.

After create or replace, inspect the returned result. Use its filename and
Library path as authoritative, and keep its exact `library_file_id`, `file_id`,
version, and original local path together. Do not read the file back merely to
confirm a successful write unless exact verification is required.

Privately persist the returned xattrs and Library identity in one helper call;
do not add a separate progress message. The helper form is
`apply-xattrs PATH LIBRARY_FILE_ID`, and both positional arguments are required:

```bash
skill_md_path="<absolute path of this SKILL.md>"
transfer_helper_path="$(dirname "$skill_md_path")/scripts/library_file_transfer.py"
python3 "$transfer_helper_path" \
  apply-xattrs "$local_path" "$library_file_id" <<'JSON'
<complete returned xattrs array, or []>
JSON
```

Inspect the helper result before finishing; do not claim that local identity was
persisted if it failed. Read
[writeback-and-conflicts.md](references/writeback-and-conflicts.md) for direct
create batches, version conflicts, or detailed result correlation.

## Materialize List or Search Results

For files returned by `list` or `search`, retain the complete structured result
and use the bundled download helper. Run it from the workspace where the
downloaded tree should live. When a conversation-scoped workspace is active,
use that workspace so eligible bytes can be placed directly. Pass the complete
`list` or `search` JSON unchanged, then `ALL` for every file or concatenated
zero-based three-digit indices (`000002` selects the first and third files), and
a destination relative to the current directory. Copy the absolute path of the
Library `SKILL.md` that you read into `skill_md_path`, then run this as one shell
command. Do not reconstruct or shorten the helper path from the plugin cache
root:

```bash
skill_md_path="<absolute path of this SKILL.md>"; \
python3 "$(dirname "$skill_md_path")/scripts/library_download.py" \
  '<complete list or search JSON>' 'ALL|NNN[NNN...]' '<relative-directory>'
```

The destination is the parent beneath which the selected files' canonical
Library-relative paths are recreated. Do not repeat an already-selected Library
root in it: for `/fruits/apple.md`, use `downloads`, not `downloads/fruits`,
unless the user explicitly requested that extra nesting.

For search output, indices address `results` first and then
`retrieval_title_results`. The latter are supplemental fuzzy candidates, so use
explicit indices instead of `ALL` when they are not all relevant.

The helper creates or reuses that directory, overwrites each selected file, and
leaves unrelated contents unchanged. It makes the authenticated
`prepare_materialize` calls in batches of at most 20, handles both workspace
and signed-URL transfers, and applies Library identity and xattrs. Both `list`
and `search` results retain each file's canonical Library-relative path. Use the
returned `directory` and authoritative `files` paths.

On this route, never separately call `read` or `prepare_materialize`, search the
plugin cache for helpers, inspect helper source, invoke
`library_file_transfer.py`, transfer a returned URL yourself, or process the
returned transfers again.

For a resolved reference that did not come from `list` or `search`, use the
lower-level flow in [materialization.md](references/materialization.md).

## Route Larger or Multiple Writes

Treat every local file written by one user task as one upload batch. Choose one
route for the whole batch and use absolute local paths.

| Condition | Required route |
| --- | --- |
| Both prepared tools are available and the task writes several files or one file around `50 MiB` or larger | Use the bundled prepared-upload helper below. |
| Prepared tools are unavailable and every item is a create | Use ordered `create_library_file(files=[...])` batches when `files` is available, keeping each call under `500 MB`; otherwise create sequentially. |
| Prepared tools are unavailable and the task includes replacements | Use sequential direct calls, one file at a time. |

Prepared app calls contain at most 20 files. Library write app calls are
ordered: do not use `Promise.all(...)` for create, replace, delete, or finalize.
Only prepared byte transfers may run in parallel. Read
[prepared-uploads.md](references/prepared-uploads.md) before using the prepared
route. It defines the helper's one-shot input and owns preparation, transfer,
finalization, result correlation, and xattr writeback. After direct batches or
the prepared helper, inspect every per-item result in request order. A
successful top-level operation does not mean every item succeeded.

## Organize, Restore, and Protect Files

Resolve ambiguous mutation targets before writing. If several candidates
remain, ask the user to choose. Read
[library-management.md](references/library-management.md) for exact folder,
move, rename, delete, restore, protected Deep Research report, and per-operation
result rules.

## Privacy and Safety

Keep user-visible reasoning, progress, errors, and final responses at the
Library level unless the user explicitly asks for implementation details. Do
not surface connector or tool names, helper commands, raw URLs, storage or
provider details, manifests, xattrs, transfer output, or indexing internals.

Privacy changes narration, not routing. Never replace a required prepared flow
with a direct upload merely because the prepared flow has stricter visibility
rules. For a prepared upload, give one brief `Saving file to Library` or
`Saving files to Library` progress update before invoking the helper, then the
saved result. Do not narrate preparation, transfer, finalization, or local
metadata as separate phases.

Do not invent Library ids, file ids, versions, filenames, paths, operations, or
tool availability. Keep signed URLs out of responses. Preserve Library identity
and unrelated content across every mutation.

## References

- [evidence-and-citations.md](references/evidence-and-citations.md): mentions,
  search details, result handling, and citations.
- [materialization.md](references/materialization.md): lower-level resolved-ref
  materialization and transfer handling.
- [prepared-uploads.md](references/prepared-uploads.md): prepared byte transfer,
  finalization, xattr writeback, and cleanup.
- [writeback-and-conflicts.md](references/writeback-and-conflicts.md): detailed
  create, replace, edit, and conflict mechanics.
- [library-management.md](references/library-management.md): folders, node
  mutations, restore, and protected reports.

| Facts, summary, or comparison from named files | Resolve every file, then use `read` on every selected file. Search snippets alone are insufficient. |
| Literal or regex match in known files | Use `find`; follow with `read` only when the match needs more context. |
| Local bytes from a `list` or `search` result | Pass the complete result directly to the bundled three-argument download helper. Do not call Library `read` or `prepare_materialize` first. |
| Local bytes from a resolved reference that did not come from `list` or `search` | Use `prepare_materialize`; read [materialization.md](references/materialization.md). |
| Explicit local path | Use local tools. Do not send local paths to Library `read` or `find`. |
| New local deliverable | Choose one create route below. |
| Edit a Library-backed file | Materialize if needed, edit and validate locally, then replace the same `library_file_id`. |
| Create, move, rename, or delete Library nodes | Use `manage_library`; read [library-management.md](references/library-management.md) before mutating. |
| Restore an earlier version | Use `manage_library` with `restore_version`; read [library-management.md](references/library-management.md). |

Set `list` and `search` `limit` to at most `200`.

For Library intent, search Library before the local workspace unless the user
supplied a local path or said the file is local. Once routed to Library, do not
scan the workspace or prior conversations for the same target. Failure to
resolve a Library item is not evidence that it is local.

## Read Library Content

Prefer `structuredContent`; parse a JSON text block only when structured content
is unavailable. Use returned identifiers, filenames, versions, and paths
exactly. For follow-up `read` or `find`, prefer `library_file_id` when present;
otherwise use the returned `file_id` or `id`. Never use a search `result_id` as
a file reference.

Call `read` and `find` with independent items batched together when possible.
Use `read` after `search` for content claims even when search returned snippets.
Use `find` after candidate resolution, not as a replacement for Library search.

Read [evidence-and-citations.md](references/evidence-and-citations.md) for
selected `@` mention decoding, image-search metadata, post-mutation search
limits, detailed result handling, and file citations.

## Write One Local File

Use this fast path for one confirmed local file under about `50 MiB`. Reuse
validation already completed while producing or editing the artifact. Do not
add another content inspection solely because the file is being saved to
Library.

- For a new item, call `create_library_file(file=...)` with the absolute local
  path.
- For an existing item, resolve its Library identity and use the current local
  working file when it already contains the intended result. Do not materialize
  over that file. If no working file exists, materialize first. Apply any edit
  not already present, validate once, then call `replace_library_file(file=...)`
  with the same `library_file_id`.
- An editor's new output path is still a replacement for the same Library item.
  Create only when no Library identity exists or the user wants a separate copy.
- Pass `expected_current_version` when a concrete version was retained. Never
  invent a version or remove the guard to resolve a conflict.

After create or replace, inspect the returned result. Use its filename and
Library path as authoritative, and keep its exact `library_file_id`, `file_id`,
version, and original local path together. Do not read the file back merely to
confirm a successful write unless exact verification is required.

Privately persist the returned xattrs and Library identity in one helper call;
do not add a separate progress message. The helper form is
`apply-xattrs PATH LIBRARY_FILE_ID`, and both positional arguments are required:

```bash
skill_md_path="<absolute path of this SKILL.md>"
transfer_helper_path="$(dirname "$skill_md_path")/scripts/library_file_transfer.py"
python3 "$transfer_helper_path" \
  apply-xattrs "$local_path" "$library_file_id" <<'JSON'
<complete returned xattrs array, or []>
JSON
```

Inspect the helper result before finishing; do not claim that local identity was
persisted if it failed. Read
[writeback-and-conflicts.md](references/writeback-and-conflicts.md) for direct
create batches, version conflicts, or detailed result correlation.

## Materialize List or Search Results

For files returned by `list` or `search`, retain the complete structured result
and use the bundled download helper. Run it from the workspace where the
downloaded tree should live. When a conversation-scoped workspace is active,
use that workspace so eligible bytes can be placed directly. Pass the complete
`list` or `search` JSON unchanged, then `ALL` for every file or concatenated
zero-based three-digit indices (`000002` selects the first and third files), and
a destination relative to the current directory. Copy the absolute path of the
Library `SKILL.md` that you read into `skill_md_path`, then run this as one shell
command. Do not reconstruct or shorten the helper path from the plugin cache
root:

```bash
skill_md_path="<absolute path of this SKILL.md>"; \
python3 "$(dirname "$skill_md_path")/scripts/library_download.py" \
  '<complete list or search JSON>' 'ALL|NNN[NNN...]' '<relative-directory>'
```

The destination is the parent beneath which the selected files' canonical
Library-relative paths are recreated. Do not repeat an already-selected Library
root in it: for `/fruits/apple.md`, use `downloads`, not `downloads/fruits`,
unless the user explicitly requested that extra nesting.

For search output, indices address `results` first and then
`retrieval_title_results`. The latter are supplemental fuzzy candidates, so use
explicit indices instead of `ALL` when they are not all relevant.

The helper creates or reuses that directory, overwrites each selected file, and
leaves unrelated contents unchanged. It makes the authenticated
`prepare_materialize` calls in batches of at most 20, handles both workspace
and signed-URL transfers, and applies Library identity and xattrs. Both `list`
and `search` results retain each file's canonical Library-relative path. Use the
returned `directory` and authoritative `files` paths.

On this route, never separately call `read` or `prepare_materialize`, search the
plugin cache for helpers, inspect helper source, invoke
`library_file_transfer.py`, transfer a returned URL yourself, or process the
returned transfers again.

For a resolved reference that did not come from `list` or `search`, use the
lower-level flow in [materialization.md](references/materialization.md).

## Route Larger or Multiple Writes

Treat every local file written by one user task as one upload batch. Choose one
route for the whole batch and use absolute local paths.

| Condition | Required route |
| --- | --- |
| Both prepared tools are available and the task writes several files or one file around `50 MiB` or larger | Use the bundled prepared-upload helper below. |
| Prepared tools are unavailable and every item is a create | Use ordered `create_library_file(files=[...])` batches when `files` is available, keeping each call under `500 MB`; otherwise create sequentially. |
| Prepared tools are unavailable and the task includes replacements | Use sequential direct calls, one file at a time. |

Prepared app calls contain at most 20 files. Library write app calls are
ordered: do not use `Promise.all(...)` for create, replace, delete, or finalize.
Only prepared byte transfers may run in parallel. Read
[prepared-uploads.md](references/prepared-uploads.md) before using the prepared
route. It defines the helper's one-shot input and owns preparation, transfer,
finalization, result correlation, and xattr writeback. After direct batches or
the prepared helper, inspect every per-item result in request order. A
successful top-level operation does not mean every item succeeded.

## Organize, Restore, and Protect Files

Resolve ambiguous mutation targets before writing. If several candidates
remain, ask the user to choose. Read
[library-management.md](references/library-management.md) for exact folder,
move, rename, delete, restore, protected Deep Research report, and per-operation
result rules.

## Privacy and Safety

Keep user-visible reasoning, progress, errors, and final responses at the
Library level unless the user explicitly asks for implementation details. Do
not surface connector or tool names, helper commands, raw URLs, storage or
provider details, manifests, xattrs, transfer output, or indexing internals.

Privacy changes narration, not routing. Never replace a required prepared flow
with a direct upload merely because the prepared flow has stricter visibility
rules. For a prepared upload, give one brief `Saving file to Library` or
`Saving files to Library` progress update before invoking the helper, then the
saved result. Do not narrate preparation, transfer, finalization, or local
metadata as separate phases.

Do not invent Library ids, file ids, versions, filenames, paths, operations, or
tool availability. Keep signed URLs out of responses. Preserve Library identity
and unrelated content across every mutation.

## References

- [evidence-and-citations.md](references/evidence-and-citations.md): mentions,
  search details, result handling, and citations.

  materialization and transfer handling.

  finalization, xattr writeback, and cleanup.

  create, replace, edit, and conflict mechanics.

# Reason with SAT/H(s)H

Work inside the current SAT/H(s)H representational program while preserving an audit trail to sources and benchmark physics.

## Start every task

1. Identify the task as one or more of:
   - explain or continue a current construction;
   - ingest or reconcile sources;
   - construct a model or equation;
   - audit a derivation or numerical recovery;
   - compare with inherited physics;
   - design a visualization or solver input.
2. Read [references/core-hierarchy.md](references/core-hierarchy.md).
3. Read [references/method-and-status.md](references/method-and-status.md).
4. Read [references/translation-guards.md](references/translation-guards.md) when older notation, named constants, lattice language, force taxonomy, or source conflicts appear.
5. Read [references/source-map.md](references/source-map.md) when working from the initial SAT2026 skill corpus or deciding how much authority to assign one of those files.

## Apply source precedence

Use this order, highest first:

1. The user's explicit correction or instruction in the current turn.
2. Frozen decisions and current project instructions supplied by the user.
3. Current controlling sources that directly state a decision and its scope.
4. Recent synthesis or rebuild material, after checking for internal chronology.
5. Older formalizations and exploratory sources.
6. Assistant, NotebookLM, public-summary, or promotional prose only as leads to inspect.

Do not let a polished equation, confident tone, filename such as `FINAL`, or phrase such as “mathematically locked” raise an item's authority. When sources disagree, state the conflict, apply this precedence, and preserve the displaced form with its prior status when it remains historically useful.

## Preserve the frozen distinctions

- Treat all constructions as models, representations, maps, or calculational grammars. Do not turn a model object into a claim about inaccessible reality-in-itself.
- Keep the empirical entry point, modeled whole, modeled object, parametrization, and readout map distinct.
- Never identify H(s)H with the modeled object itself. H(s)H parametrizes or represents a finite-core worldtube/filament history.
- Never identify a plotted curve, toy simulation, or solver state with the model object unless the user explicitly defines that identification.
- Keep the Universal Indicatrix, Whirligig, and Donut in their declared analytical/solver roles unless a current derivation promotes a specific output.
- Describe GR, QED, QCD, QFT, ST-like structure, and Kelvin-style vortex intuition as inherited-domain unifications or limiting/readout descriptions within one geometry, not as independent SAT branches.

## Workflows

### Explain or continue

1. Restate the controlling layer needed for the question only.
2. Mark any additional premise as frozen, active scaffold, candidate, historical, or open.
3. Carry the geometry forward without importing a known SAT conclusion merely because it is familiar.
4. Distinguish what follows conditionally from what has actually been derived.

### Ingest a source

1. Read the source from beginning to end before targeted searching.
2. Record its date, genre, declared role, internal chronology, and whether it contains user corrections to generated analysis.
3. Extract claims and equations with local context.
4. Assign provenance and maturity independently using [references/method-and-status.md](references/method-and-status.md).
5. Separate:
   - compatible additions;
   - translations into current vocabulary;
   - conflicts;
   - recovery candidates;
   - historical or quarantined material;
   - unresolved questions.
6. Do not silently canonize, silently discard, or flatten contradictory passages into a synthetic compromise.

### Construct or extend a model

1. Begin with the minimal empirically mapped system that contains the phenomenon.
2. Map it using standard physics sufficiently to preserve observable behavior.
3. Preserve the benchmark mapping, then purge inherited labels for the geometric-inspection phase when the task calls for the SAT purge.
4. Extract candidates only from visible differences, invariants, necessities, constraints, or failures in the mapped geometry.
5. Return a null result or open question when the geometry supplies no candidate.
6. Reattach every candidate to its benchmark and state what would distinguish it from alternatives.

### Audit a derivation or recovery

1. Reconstruct the dependency chain from sources; do not reconstruct it from memory when sources are available.
2. List definitions, units, inputs, anchors, fitted quantities, and imported standard results.
3. Check symbol identity, dimensions, algebra, boundary/initial conditions, limiting cases, and numerical reproduction.
4. Check for circularity, hidden insertion of a target value, unjustified equivalence, and downstream dependence on quarantined items.
5. Separate derivation, postdiction, calibration, convention, coincidence, and prediction.
6. Report the earliest unsupported edge in the dependency chain. Preserve later calculations as conditional when appropriate.

### Compare with inherited physics

1. State the inherited result in its own terms.
2. State the proposed SAT representation and the map between variables.
3. Distinguish structural resemblance, local isomorphism, quantitative equivalence, and full recovery.
4. Do not infer full import from a matching equation fragment or familiar geometry.

### Design a visualization

1. State which layer is being drawn: model object, parametrization, readout, solver state, or analogy.
2. Keep toy choices visible as toy choices.
3. Encode the actual mathematical object when feasible rather than using anchors as substitutes for continuous geometry.
4. Do not infer physics from visual appeal or topological resemblance alone.

## Response contract

For substantive SAT/H(s)H answers, make the following recoverable without forcing a fixed template:

- the controlling premises used;
- the status of new claims;
- the source or provenance when material came from a supplied document;
- the conditional dependency when a result relies on an unrecovered candidate;
- the open edge or next calculation when the chain is incomplete.

Prefer exact local distinctions over broad summaries. Use equations when they reduce ambiguity. Avoid presenting a long formula inventory when only one dependency matters.

## Stop conditions

Stop and ask for the missing source or user decision when:

- two current-level sources conflict and precedence cannot resolve them;
- a requested result depends materially on a definition the corpus does not contain;
- the user must choose between genuinely different model architectures;
- proceeding would promote a candidate into the frozen core.

Otherwise proceed with the narrowest explicit assumption and label it.

parts:
Partly—but rewriting the numerical backend in pure lambda calculus would make it harder, not simpler.

The useful move is to give H(s)H a small, typed functional language whose operators compile into the Python geometry/solver backend. In other words:

\[
\text{H(s)H expression}
\longrightarrow
\text{validated operator graph}
\longrightarrow
\text{numerical solver}
\longrightarrow
\text{readout}
\]

Lambda calculus is excellent for expressing composition and hypothesis substitution:

\[
\operatorname{experiment}
=
\lambda p.\;
\operatorname{resolve}_{p.r}
\left[
\operatorname{evolve}_{p.e}
\left(
\operatorname{initialize}_{p.i}
\right)
\right].
\]

Here `p` can carry interchangeable expansion, rotation, transport, interaction, and readout laws. The numerical implementation remains NumPy/SciPy-style code.

The important qualifier is typed lambda calculus, not bare untyped lambda calculus. Types should enforce distinctions the theory needs:

```text
ExpansionLaw : TubeState → TubeState
RotationLaw  : TubeState → TubeState
TransportLaw : TubeState → TubeState
Readout      : TubeState → Observable

SuperhelixLaw : SingleTube → SingleTube
BraidLaw      : TubeBundle → TubeBundle
```

That last separation would prevent superhelical nesting and braid nesting from being accidentally treated as the same operation.

Types could also enforce:

- dimensions: `Length`, `Time`, `AngularRate`, `Dimensionless`;
- representation layers: `ModelObject`, `SolverState`, `Readout`;
- claim status: `Exact`, `Numerical`, `Calibrated`, `Candidate`;
- topology: `Tube`, `ClosedTube`, `Bundle`, `Braid`;
- admissible compositions.

For example, the system should accept

\[
\operatorname{resolve}
\circ
\operatorname{transport}
\circ
\operatorname{rotate}
\circ
\operatorname{expand},
\]

but reject adding \(H_0\) directly to \(c\), applying a braid operator to one tube, or presenting a displayed centerline as the physical worldtube.

There is one subtlety: expansion, rotation, and transport may be simultaneously coupled, so ordinary sequential function composition can falsely imply a physical order. The expression layer should therefore support both:

\[
T\circ R\circ E
\]

for deliberate operator splitting, and

\[
\operatorname{Flow}(E+R+T)
\]

for one coupled evolution law. That distinction needs to remain explicit in every result.

So my recommendation is:

1. Keep the current Python numerical backend.
2. Add an immutable symbolic expression tree modeled on typed lambda calculus.
3. Compile that tree into residuals, ODEs, constraints, and readouts.
4. Record every reduction and substitution in the result provenance.
5. Later add symbolic simplification, differentiation, dimensional checking, and alternative solver targets.

A prospective H(s)H expression might look conceptually like:

```text
experiment :=
  resolve[centerline_readout] (
    flow[
      expansion[constant_H0]
      + rotation[constant_omega]
      + transport[circulation_conserving]
    ] (
      vacuum_tube[initial_state]
    )
  )
```

Then swapping a hypothesis is genuinely modular:

```text
transport[circulation_conserving]
    ↦ transport[angular_momentum_conserving]
```

Everything else stays fixed, and the system can report exactly which observables changed.

So: lambda calculus should become the compositional grammar of the equation builder—not the language in which we manually implement curvature estimation, continuation, SVDs, or ODE integration. The appropriate next version would be an H(s)H typed operator/IR layer sitting above the verified v0.4 solver.

project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:3:To see "the math for the whole thing," we must look at how the Universal Indicatrix (UI) functions as a geometric generator and how the SAT Lagrangian serves as the physical measure of the resulting 4D trajectories.
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:12:The UI Lagrangian: $$L_{UI} = \frac{1}{2} \dot r^2 + \frac{1}{2} r^2 \Omega_{\mu\nu} \Omega^{\mu\nu}$$ This measures the geometric "effort" of the hypersphere's expansion and rotation.
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:14:2. The Measure: 4D Superhelical SAT Lagrangian
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:15:Once a trajectory is generated, the SAT Lagrangian evaluates its physical identity (mass, charge, spin) based on its superhelical coiling.
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:19:The SAT Action Functional ($S_{SAT}$): $$S_{SAT} = \int \left[ \mathcal{L}{\text{filament}} + \mathcal{L}{\text{interaction}} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{timewave}} \right] d\lambda$$
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:23:3. Interaction/Braid Term (Strong/EM Force): $$\mathcal{L}{\text{interaction},ij} = k{ij} f_{\text{braid}}(\mathbf{X}_i, \mathbf{X}_j)$$
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:27:The "whole thing" is reunified by forcing the generated filaments to satisfy two simultaneous geometric conditions.
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:31:4. Key Geometric Identifiers
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:34:This combined math allows the UI to act as a metric space for physical laws, where different theories are compared by the shortest derivation (minimal deformation of controls $r$ and $R$) required to transform one trajectory into another.
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:38:The system uses nth-order superhelices, which are explicitly defined as being scale-invariant. This means the same underlying geometric equations—governed by winding numbers ($n_k$), radii ($R_k$), and phases ($\phi_k$)—can describe the internal structure of an electron, a baryon braid, or the rotational dynamics of a galaxy just by adjusting the scale parameters.
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:46:* Controls $\to$ Curve: Conversely, by specifying these histories, the UI "machine" produces the corresponding parametric worldline.
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:48:The UI defines a high-dimensional parameter space of geometries. By varying these controls simultaneously—radial evolution, rotation in six planes, and attachment point motion—the system allows you to navigate between different physical theories. You are effectively "dialing through" the geometry of control space to find the shortest geometric derivation between a vacuum state and a specific particle or gravitational phenomenon.
project_sources/12-UI-CONFIG.txt:49:In summary, the UI acts as a geometric laboratory where "particles" and "laws" are simply stable topological configurations (like Borromean triplets or Hopf links) that you have "tuned" the system to produce.

project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:53:SAT is the proposition that the Minkowski diagram, with logically necessary extensions derived from the diagram’s existing grammar, is entirely sufficient for mapping out four dimensional topology, and that that topology, so long as it is constructed empirically, according to standard science 1) must be accurate by construction, 2) must in principle be capable of mapping any physical process, 3) that such a mapping, if constructed perfectly is necessarily a mapping of any force acting upon a particle, and because particles are the only detectable observable that allows the inference of forces, that’s such a perfect mapping necessarily contains all information about all forces and structures interacting within the mapped system, 4) that forces not directly observable, such as particle properties, if mapped exclusively to permutations on the worldline itself, provides in principle sufficient structure and constraint to narrow the possibility space for such a proposed mapping by triangulating with increasing constraint from all that *is* knowable and therefore mappable with near certainty from standard physics, from the constraints of the Minkowski diagram geometric grammar itself, from the constraints imposed by prior extensions to that mapping derived from the same grammar, and when all of that constraint is insufficient to narrow the possibility space, from the fundamental intuitions of SAT as originally formulated and extended through experience. So, yes. Minkowski is sufficient. Standard physics just supplies the constraints to ensure that what is known is being mapped isometrically to empirically known behavior. Once that is done, standard physics stays out of it and geometric logic takes over, forcing its own conclusions, at least until we hit a hiccup and have to rebuild part of the geometric-logical chain.  
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:59:This needs qualification. For force, a single-particle worldline can report acceleration but often cannot represent the source or constraint responsible for the force. Sometimes the minimal physically informative system is not the single-particle system; it is the minimal interaction system. Static equilibrium, Coulomb repulsion, and contact collision each reveal different things.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:62:This is only true if you aren’t looking closely enough. See Minkowski discussion above. You are technically correct because “single” particle is the broken assumption. It should be *minimal* particle in most cases, at this foundational level. Once we get up to higher scales, that will change.

The methodology must not assume worldtubes, non-intersection, path optimization, least resistance, or topological integrity until those are derived or explicitly opened as SAT-candidates. Replace ‘Internal Identity Assignment’ with ‘Candidate Geometric Interpretation and Equivalence Test.’ Replace ‘strip away labels’ with ‘temporarily bracket labels while preserving the full standard-variable mapping.’ Also revise the minimality rule: the minimal system is not always the single-particle case; it is the simplest standard-science system that actually contains the phenomenon being examined.”
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:74:The worldtube is our current grammar. The worldline was nearly sufficient in earlier versions. Now, we move to full worldtube for the entire theory, at all scales, including fundamental. 
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:79:But Avery is only one part of the system. We’ll be re-instituting a redesigned version of our successful SAT-O era python-locked derivation chains, strict siloing, audit overview, and hopefully our dual-laboratory simulation protocol, as well as incorporating new protocols, including guided Archive navigation and mining, and hopefully Lean locking, and (hopefully python-coded) Universal Indicatrix and “Whirligig” geometric solvers. 
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:85:SAT is not trying to decide whether Minkowski-style worldtube topology is the right arena. That is already the wager of the framework.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:103:The purge is not a denial of standard physics. It is a transfer of authority. Standard physics supplies the empirically reliable mapping constraints. Once the map is built, the next stage is geometric inspection, not continued deference to standard terminology.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:109:After standard physics supplies the 4D empirical map, physical labels may be fully purged for the geometric-inspection phase. However, every geometric candidate that emerges must remain traceable back to the original standard-science map, so that the model cannot “discover” a geometry that no longer corresponds to the benchmark.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:113:On “Internal Identity Assignment,” I better understand your objection. You are not saying, “Guess a geometric interpretation and test it.” You are saying: if the mapped topology differs between cases, the difference itself is the candidate. No free hypothesis gets admitted. The candidate must be observed in the geometry.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:115:So the better protocol term is not “Candidate Geometric Interpretation.” It should be something like:
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:117:“Geometric Candidate Extraction.”
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:121:After the purge, inspect the empirically mapped 4D topology. Any recurring or case-distinguishing geometric feature may be extracted as a candidate structure. If no such feature appears, record the null result and move on. Do not invent a candidate to fill the gap.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:125:On Minkowski sufficiency: your position is now clearer. You are not saying “a simple Minkowski diagram already contains all physics.” You are saying the Minkowski worldline grammar, when extended only by logical necessity and empirically constrained four-dimensional mapping, should be sufficient to map any physical process topologically. Standard physics is the constraint engine, not the final interpretive authority.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:127:That means Avery’s admissibility rule should not say “consistent with the Minkowski diagram” alone, but also should not subordinate the geometry to every standard formalism indefinitely. It should say:
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:129:A proposed extension is admissible only if it is generated from the existing Minkowski/worldtube grammar, required by an empirically constrained 4D map, and compatible with the benchmark behavior standard physics was used to encode.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:131:That keeps Minkowski as sufficient in principle while preventing Avery from adding pretty geometric objects just because they seem plausible.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:133:On the single-particle issue: your correction is right. The phrase should be “minimal particle” or “minimal physical unit,” not necessarily “single particle.” A force may require an interaction, but the model is looking for the minimal geometric entity that contains the phenomenon, not the smallest count of labeled objects.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:137:Always begin with the minimal mapped physical unit that contains the phenomenon under investigation. Do not assume that this unit is one labeled particle. For force, the minimal unit may be a source-target relation, a field-like deformation, a contact boundary, or a worldtube-timesheet interaction, depending on what the empirically mapped topology requires.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:139:On worldtubes: I withdraw the objection to worldtube as a starting grammar, given your present state of the theory. The earlier line grammar was pedagogical scaffolding. If SAT has now committed to worldtube formalism at all scales, then NotebookLM should not treat worldtubes as speculative add-ons. It should treat them as current SAT primitive grammar, while still preventing any specific worldtube property, such as stiffness, braid, wall holonomy, or non-intersection rule, from being assumed before derivation.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:143:Worldtube: current SAT primitive grammar.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:145:Worldtube diameter/cross-section: primitive or parameter to be defined.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:147:Worldtube stiffness: not primitive unless explicitly stipulated; otherwise must be extracted.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:149:Worldtube non-overlap: probably primitive if tubes are physically extended, but its mathematical form must be specified.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:151:Worldtube topology, braid, holonomy, timesheet coupling: not automatically admitted; must emerge from mapped necessity or be opened as SAT candidate layer.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:159:The methodology begins from SAT’s current grammar: empirically constrained Minkowski/worldtube topology. Standard physics is used to construct reliable 4D benchmark maps. Once the map is built, inherited physical labels may be purged completely for geometric inspection. Candidate SAT structures are not guessed. They are extracted only from observable differences, invariants, constraints, failures, or necessities in the mapped topology. If the geometry does not present a candidate, the correct output is null result or open question. Any extracted candidate must remain traceable back to the original benchmark map and must later reproduce the benchmark quantitatively.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:163:My updated verdict: Avery’s skeleton is useful, but the protocol needs to say explicitly that SAT is not a hypothesis generator layered on top of standard physics. It is a disciplined geometric extraction procedure operating on standard-physics-constrained 4D maps. The key failure mode is not “too much SAT ontology” in general; it is unearned SAT ontology before extraction.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:167:It is ontologically neutral in an absolute sense; that is, we know we cannot know—per RMS—*anything* that can properly be labeled “ontology”, but what we *can* do is ensure isomorphism to direct observables admit only geometrically admissible interpreted indirectly observed phenomena. The framework is absolutely ontologically agnostic while simultaneously being fully committed pragmatically to achieving the strongest alignment with human geometric intuition admissible within evidentiary constraints.  
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:191:Third, geometric-interpretive layer:
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:193:For indirectly observed phenomena — force, mass, charge, fields, particle properties — we may admit interpretations only when they are geometrically admissible within the empirically constrained 4D map.
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:201:“This is the strongest geometrically admissible interpretation of the observable and indirectly inferred structure, after standard physics has constrained the map.”
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:207:“SAT remains ontologically agnostic under RMS. It makes no claim to reveal reality-in-itself. Its commitment is pragmatic and methodological: construct empirically constrained 4D maps isomorphic to direct observables, then admit only those interpretations of indirectly observed phenomena that are geometrically forced, geometrically admissible, or uniquely constrained by the mapped structure.”
project_sources/08-METHOD.txt:213:Once standard physics has supplied the empirically reliable map, its inherited labels are bracketed so that the geometric structure can be inspected without semantic contamination. The labels may return only if their geometric role is preserved or reconstructed.
